title: Humanitarian Corridors Under Siege: Mariupol 2022
summary: A retrospective decision-support prototype that scores daily danger and evacuation feasibility for civilians during the 2022 siege of Mariupol, anchored in international humanitarian law.

contribution.roleNote: Ethical Tech CoLab fork of ChristineLumen/mariupol-evacuation-model; Yorke advised.

narrative.problem: During the siege of Mariupol, 5 March – 20 May 2022, civilians faced daily danger from hostilities, deprivation and infrastructure destruction, while the negotiated evacuation mechanism envisaged by GC IV art. 17 arrived only on 30 April.
narrative.decision: Combines six normalised severity components with a generalised power mean (p = 6, weakest-link), so the worst component drives the daily score instead of being averaged away, and pairs it with a satellite-based feasibility axis.
narrative.tradeoff: The exponent, normalisation bounds and phase thresholds are documented conventions, and the sensitivity analysis shows two results, 'violence never dominates' and the Critical phase, do not survive alternative settings.
narrative.limitation: Retrospective and only partially validated against observed displacement; event reporting degrades inside the besieged city as severity peaks, and district demographics in the feasibility axis are author's estimates.
narrative.caveat: Retrospective research prototype, not operational guidance. Front lines and damage zones are approximate, and the same data fusion that prioritises evacuation could support targeting.
